A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same K-12 RAG robustness benchmark, renamed from EDUKDQA to KnowShiftQA. Text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison; appendices A–G are retained and v2 adds Appendix H.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and question-answering experiments, evaluations before and after hypothetical knowledge updates, and a prompting comparison in Tables 2–4 and 8–10.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and additionally reports manual-curation outcomes in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The hypothetical-update procedure, question typology, curation pipeline, and Locate-and-Answer prompting remain unchanged. Added explanations of distant-question construction and existing Contriever fine-tuning do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The renamed dataset retains 3,005 questions, 2,205 documents, the same five subjects and question types, and the same original-versus-updated knowledge scenarios. Appendix A's textbook sources and Tables 6–7's coverage statistics are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same 11 retrieval entries and 16 LLMs. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the end-to-end RAG and prompting comparisons in Tables 4 and 10. Newly cited related work is not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Paragraph retrieval, recall@1/5, QA accuracy, zero-shot Locate-and-Answer evaluation, and the before/after knowledge-update comparison remain unchanged. The newly stated 200-word minimum for Multi-hop Distant documents and contrastive fine-tuning describe existing experiments without revising a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: The knowledge-update robustness comparison, subject/type breakdowns, and direct-answer versus Locate-and-Answer comparison are retained. Appendix H interprets existing results rather than adding an ablation, robustness experiment, or error-analysis dataset.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added curation percentages are outcome rates, not uncertainty estimates; v2's use of 'significant' introduces no statistical test.

E6.justification: All numerical table entries are unchanged. Appendix B newly reports that 90.5% of queries were retained or slightly refined, with an overall success rate of 86.4%. Appendix H also highlights a previously undiscussed Simple Direct ranking pattern using the existing Table 3 results.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The reasoning-pattern diagrams and question typology are retained; the added description of distant facts supplies operational curation detail rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a benchmark for textbook–LLM knowledge discrepancies, substantial RAG performance degradation, and difficulty integrating contextual and parametric knowledge. The new title and terminology preserve this scope. v2's introduction emphasizes fine-tuning benefits already stated in v1 Section 3.1.

C2.justification: New Appendix H proposes excessive confidence in parametric knowledge as an explanation for otherwise stronger models' weaker Simple Direct performance. It expands the distinction between factual correctness and following authoritative context, and discusses applicability when real-world ground truth is ambiguous. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a repository link where v1 promised future release. Appendices B–C newly disclose the distant-fact selection description, the 200-word document minimum, and contrastive learning for the already reported Contriever fine-tuning. These improve documentation without establishing changed experiments; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds brief connections to vector/neural graph databases, abductive and inductive reasoning, and factuality versus instruction following. Appendix B adds logical-reasoning references motivating the typology. These extend the literature discussion while retaining the original research gap and positioning.

P1.justification: The title and dataset name change, and the abstract and several introductory and experimental paragraphs are rewritten or clarified. Acknowledgments and Appendix H are added, and Appendix G's mistaken Table 3 reference is corrected to Table 10. The main section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The appendix layout is substantially reorganized from two-column prose with Tables 5–10 collected on the final page to single-column pages distributing those tables alongside their relevant discussions. Figure 2 moves below the textbook list. The three figures and ten tables retain their substantive contents.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through the repository pointer and curation/fine-tuning details, and improves navigation by integrating appendix tables with their discussions and correcting the Table 10 reference. Appendix H adds useful interpretive qualifications, although its calibration explanation remains untested. The unchanged benchmark evidence and limited additional curation reporting support a modest overall improvement.
